section_summary: This section concerns exchange rates, blocked yen, and the use of Japanese currency during the occupation. Much of the correspondence addresses requests to release Italian and French funds in Japan or convert private yen holdings into dollars. Later papers consider how missionaries, publishers, and news services could operate without creating further claims for dollar conversion.

subfiles.title: Draft recommendations on exchange rates for Japanese outlying islands
subfiles.about: Forwards draft recommendations following an interdepartmental meeting on an exchange rate for the Japanese outlying islands.
subfiles.summary: Forwards draft rate recommendations after the January 2 meeting.

subfiles.title: Alternative courses on outlying islands and Formosa exchange rates
subfiles.about: Weighs negotiations with Treasury over proposed five-, eight-, and ten-cent rates for the outlying islands and Formosa.
subfiles.summary: Recommends seeking a high-level compromise with Treasury before abandoning further negotiations. The paper treats Formosa’s eventual rate as politically significant.

subfiles.title: Letter on yen needed for troop pay in Japan
subfiles.about: Advises planning for enough yen to pay troops at twenty yen per dollar without fixing a permanent exchange rate.
subfiles.summary: Recommends holding currency sufficient for troop pay at twenty yen per dollar.

subfiles.title: Japanese rate of exchange for troop pay
subfiles.about: Compares Treasury’s five-cent troop-pay rate with State’s proposed ten-cent rate.
subfiles.summary: Explains the competing rates and asks for a political decision on which to recommend.

subfiles.title: Italian request to release gold bullion in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests release of Bank of Italy gold held at the Bank of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks that 213 kilograms of blocked Italian gold be included among assets sought for release.

subfiles.title: Urgent request concerning Italian officials’ blocked funds
subfiles.about: Urges action to let Italian officials in Japan use blocked funds.
subfiles.summary: Reports increasing hardship and asks Dowling to press U.S. military authorities for a decision.

subfiles.title: Indelli telegram on permission to use Italian funds
subfiles.about: Seeks confirmation that U.S. authorities have authorized use of Italian funds in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Says permission reportedly granted in Washington has not reached headquarters in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Acheson request to investigate Italian funds
subfiles.about: Relays Acheson’s request to examine what can be done about Italian funds in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks for investigation of the Italian funds issue.

subfiles.title: Telephone-conversation transmittal
subfiles.about: Transmits material following telephone conversations.
subfiles.summary: Brief transmittal referring to earlier calls.

subfiles.title: Briefing on Italian ambassador’s expected discussion
subfiles.about: Previews Tarchiani’s likely requests concerning Italy’s armistice and foreign relations.
subfiles.summary: Anticipates discussion of armistice revision, Spain, and Argentina.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Italian Ambassador Tarchiani
subfiles.about: Records discussion of Italian funds in Japan and several European diplomatic issues.
subfiles.summary: Tarchiani requests help for former internees whose funds in Japan are frozen. He also discusses French-Italian relations, armistice revision, and continued civilian supplies to Italy.

subfiles.title: Italian memorandum on frozen funds in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests equitable treatment of Italian government and private funds frozen in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Warns that freezing funds obstructs repatriation and assistance for former Italian internees.

subfiles.title: Rome telegram on blocked Italian funds
subfiles.about: Reports an Italian request to unblock funds in Japan and China.
subfiles.summary: The Italian Foreign Office seeks access to local currency and transferable funds for sailors, communities, and diplomatic personnel. The embassy asks for information to answer it.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Rome on Italian assets in Japan
subfiles.about: Explains U.S. policy on Italian yen accounts, foreign currency, gold, and repatriation.
subfiles.summary: Permits limited use of yen for Italian personnel and nationals, with broader access for Italians in good standing. Foreign currency and gold remain blocked, and repatriates face limits on what they may take.

subfiles.title: Italian ambassador’s appeal quoting Indelli
subfiles.about: Requests release of Italian government, official, and private funds in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Quotes Indelli on unpaid salaries, debts, and hardship, then seeks an early U.S. response.

subfiles.title: Ortona letter on Italian funds in Tokyo
subfiles.about: Asks why authorization to use Italian funds has not reached U.S. headquarters in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Repeats Indelli’s telegram and asks for information and relief for distressed Italians.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on blocked Italian assets
subfiles.about: Summarizes U.S. rules governing Italian yen, foreign currency, gold, and personal effects.
subfiles.summary: The draft allows licensed use of yen accounts for subsistence, salaries, property, and repatriation. It withholds permission to dispose of foreign currency or gold in Japan and limits currency taken out by repatriates.

subfiles.title: French aide-mémoire on repatriation from East Asia
subfiles.about: Requests faster repatriation of French nationals remaining in China and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Notes that 23 French nationals from Shanghai have returned but hundreds in China still await transport in difficult conditions. It asks U.S. authorities to help accelerate departures.

subfiles.title: Fujikawa request to exchange yen
subfiles.about: Asks for help converting yen into dollars after returning from Japan without funds.
subfiles.summary: Fujikawa describes her illness, lack of money, and unsuccessful attempts to receive funds from Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply to Fujikawa on yen conversion
subfiles.about: Says no facilities exist to convert her yen into dollars.
subfiles.summary: States that 1,500 yen would likely be valued at no more than $100 even if conversion were possible.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Fujikawa’s address
subfiles.about: Requests Fujikawa’s current address after a State Department reply was returned.
subfiles.summary: Asks the society for a usable address.

subfiles.title: American Baptist reply with Fujikawa’s address
subfiles.about: Provides Fujikawa’s current New York lodging address.
subfiles.summary: Reports that she is staying at Kenmore Hall.

subfiles.title: Resent reply to Fujikawa
subfiles.about: Repeats the Department’s answer about converting yen at her corrected address.
subfiles.summary: Advises that no yen-to-dollar conversion facility exists.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on Indelli’s dollar holdings
subfiles.about: Reports Indelli’s protest against limits on removing U.S. currency from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Indelli says his family depends on his dollar holdings; the telegram discusses their uncertain origin.

subfiles.title: Document charge card
subfiles.about: Records file handling information for a document in the exchange file.
subfiles.summary: Mostly blank file control card.

subfiles.title: Fujikawa address note
subfiles.about: Supplies a temporary New York address.
subfiles.summary: Gives Kenmore Hall as her address.

subfiles.title: Japanese-Italian dealings in U.S. currency in South America
subfiles.about: Reports a 1942 transaction involving Italian U.S. currency in Chile and Argentina and gold held in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Recommends investigation of the transaction and the gold earmarked for Italy.

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of Gregg’s yen inquiry
subfiles.about: Forwards Charles Gregg’s request concerning yen and his dollar obligation.
subfiles.summary: Sends Gregg’s letter to State for advice.

subfiles.title: Gregg request to apply yen against promissory notes
subfiles.about: Asks whether yen obtained while interned can offset dollar promissory notes or be exchanged.
subfiles.summary: Describes yen received through the Swiss consul in Kobe and requests a credit or dollar exchange.

subfiles.title: Payment for services in Germany and Japan
subfiles.about: Supports restricting service sales that create blocked yen or mark balances.
subfiles.summary: Reports agreement with a proposed ban on unapproved service sales in Japan paid in yen.

subfiles.title: Proposed policy on payment for Japanese imports
subfiles.about: Proposes paying for essential imports into Japan in dollars or other acceptable foreign exchange.
subfiles.summary: The paper argues that paying foreign sellers in blocked yen creates pressure for later dollar conversion. It proposes permitting only imports SCAP considers essential and paying for them in available foreign exchange.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Gregg
subfiles.about: Explains why yen cannot satisfy Gregg’s dollar promissory notes or be exchanged.
subfiles.summary: State says it cannot accept yen against obligations incurred to obtain wartime funds. Changing repayment terms would require congressional action.

subfiles.title: French yen account referred to Treasury
subfiles.about: Seeks Treasury advice on releasing yen for the French Chancery in Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the French Embassy’s request concerning its Tokyo bank account.

subfiles.title: Treasury reply on French yen balances
subfiles.about: Discusses remittances and possible release of French government yen balances in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Treasury says it can authorize new remittances and sees no objection to using existing French balances if the bank is solvent. SCAP blocking orders, rather than Treasury regulations, appear to prevent withdrawals.

subfiles.title: Conversion of yen held outside Japan
subfiles.about: Seeks guidance on requests to convert old yen held outside Japan into new Japanese currency.
subfiles.summary: Discusses large yen holdings in Korea and requests a policy directive for SCAP.

subfiles.title: Unblocking yen for French diplomatic mission
subfiles.about: Reports a French request for another five million yen and the dispatch of a cable before approval was confirmed.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the request and explains that War sent the cable after a misunderstanding.

subfiles.title: Request for War clearance of French yen cable
subfiles.about: Requests War Department clearance for a cable on French mission yen expenses.
subfiles.summary: Describes the proposed additional release and asks for clearance.

subfiles.title: Martin transmittal of French mission cable
subfiles.about: Forwards a cleared draft cable on the French mission’s request for five million yen.
subfiles.summary: Asks that the draft go to the Civil Affairs Division for transmission.

subfiles.title: Draft cable on additional French mission funds
subfiles.about: Suggests SCAP assess the French mission’s need before unblocking five million yen.
subfiles.summary: Leaves the amount released to SCAP’s judgment under existing restrictions.

subfiles.title: Duplicate memorandum on French mission yen
subfiles.about: Copies the memorandum reporting premature dispatch of the French mission cable.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the approval memorandum on page 48.

subfiles.title: Duplicate draft French mission cable
subfiles.about: Copies the proposed instruction to consider unblocking five million yen.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the draft cable on page 51.

subfiles.title: Handwritten routing note on French mission cable
subfiles.about: Notes that War dispatched the French mission cable before Hilldring’s approval was confirmed.
subfiles.summary: Records the dispatch misunderstanding and follow-up.

subfiles.title: War Department cable authorizing French yen review
subfiles.about: Instructs occupation authorities to review a request to unblock five million yen for the French mission.
subfiles.summary: Directs an investigation of need and permits action under current blocking restrictions.

subfiles.title: Exchange-rate correspondence forwarded to Martin
subfiles.about: Forwards Church World Service’s letter on Japanese and Korean currency rates.
subfiles.summary: Sends the letter for appropriate action.

subfiles.title: Church World Service on exchange-rate hardship
subfiles.about: Asks that missionary and relief agencies’ interests be considered in any currency-rate change.
subfiles.summary: Reports hardship from the current conversion rate in Japan and Korea.

subfiles.title: Hilldring reply to Church World Service
subfiles.about: Promises consideration of missionary and relief interests in currency-rate decisions.
subfiles.summary: Explains that exchange rates remain under consideration and acknowledges the agencies’ concerns.

subfiles.title: Crowell-Collier proposal to distribute magazines in Japan
subfiles.about: Seeks help licensing distribution of American magazines in Japan, with payment in yen.
subfiles.summary: Carroll describes talks with occupation officials and a proposed Japanese distributor. He asks for help with a Treasury license and says the publisher will accept yen at the authorized rate.

subfiles.title: Crowell-Collier foreign funds license application
subfiles.about: Applies for permission to pursue an international magazine project that includes Japan.
subfiles.summary: Describes a proposed locally published magazine promoting international amity, printing, travel, and trade.

subfiles.title: Crowell-Collier proposal to publish in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests help obtaining a license to negotiate Japanese publication of an international magazine.
subfiles.summary: Carroll outlines a magazine modeled on *Victory* and identifies Toppan Printing as a prospective Japanese publisher. He seeks a Treasury license for further negotiations.

subfiles.title: Martin reply to Crowell-Collier
subfiles.about: Addresses licensing, SCAP approval, and the risk of accepting yen for publications in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Supports educational publications in principle but notes Japan’s limited foreign exchange and the difficulty of converting yen earned there.

subfiles.title: Draft of Martin’s reply on publishing and yen
subfiles.about: Drafts State’s response to Crowell-Collier’s publication and licensing proposals.
subfiles.summary: Discusses Treasury and SCAP approval, scarce dollars, and the risk of accumulating yen balances.

subfiles.title: Proposed cable on French charitable institutions
subfiles.about: Proposes releasing clean yen funds for French charitable institutions in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Supports unblocking one million yen if the funds did not arise from wartime collaboration. The attached draft asks SCAP to make that distinction.

subfiles.title: Hilldring approval request on French charitable funds
subfiles.about: Submits a cleared cable on yen for French charitable institutions.
subfiles.summary: Requests Hilldring’s approval after War and Treasury concurrence.

subfiles.title: Copy of approval request on French charitable funds
subfiles.about: Copies the request to approve a cable on French charitable yen.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the memorandum on page 69.

subfiles.title: Request for War concurrence on French charitable funds
subfiles.about: Asks War to clear a revised cable on unblocking yen for French charities.
subfiles.summary: Notes Treasury concurrence and requests War’s response.

subfiles.title: Cable seeking SCAP information on French charity funds
subfiles.about: Seeks information before deciding whether to unblock one million yen for French charities.
subfiles.summary: Asks SCAP to assess the funds’ wartime origins and any conflict with liquidation controls.

subfiles.title: Referral of Schneider’s letter
subfiles.about: Refers an attorney’s inquiry about converting a Japanese bank deposit.
subfiles.summary: Sends Schneider’s letter for action.

subfiles.title: Schneider inquiry on Kanematsu’s yen deposit
subfiles.about: Asks how Thelma Kanematsu can convert or value her Japanese bank savings.
subfiles.summary: Describes a joint Yokohama bank account of about 30,000 yen and requests guidance.

subfiles.title: State reply to Schneider
subfiles.about: Responds to the inquiry about Kanematsu’s yen account and currency conversion.
subfiles.summary: Explains that Japan has exchange controls and that the account’s ownership affects what action is possible.

subfiles.title: Schneider follow-up on Kanematsu’s deposit
subfiles.about: Renews his request for information on the value and conversion of Kanematsu’s yen.
subfiles.summary: Says he has received no reply to his December letter and requests prompt guidance.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on Japanese government bond coupons
subfiles.about: Asks whether English holders can obtain payment on prewar Japanese government bond coupons.
subfiles.summary: Seeks rules for coupons held by Royal Bank of Scotland for English residents.

subfiles.title: Reply on Japanese bond coupon claims
subfiles.about: Directs English coupon holders to inquire with the Office of Alien Property.
subfiles.summary: State declines to interpret that office’s payment authority.

subfiles.title: Revised draft cable on export-import funds for reorientation
subfiles.to: Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas
subfiles.about: Requests comments on a revised cable concerning funding for news services in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a revised draft and withdraws the earlier version.

subfiles.title: Draft cable on payment for news services in Japan
subfiles.about: Proposes continued yen payment for news services because dollar trust funds cannot cover their costs.
subfiles.summary: The draft says available dollars are needed for essential imports. It proposes that news agencies accept nonconvertible yen and use it for authorized local expenses and traffic charges.
